title: Anirban Chakraborty
text:
Outside research, I enjoy several extra curricular activities, including hiking, music composition. While many of these activities are recreational in nature, they help me keep motivated and evolve myself.

Hiking
I particularly enjoy high-altitude, multi-day treks. Because such trips require early planning, finding fellow trekkers, and careful assessment of risks, they have shaped how I approach planning in research as well. They have also taught me persistence when the path forward is difficult.






Ice Lake Hike, Silverton, Colorado







Mesquite Flat Sand Dunes, Death Valley, California









Brahmatal Hike, India







Paso Rosario, Cordillera Huayhuash Circuit Trek, Perú







Music
I have a keen interest in various kinds of instrumental music. As a guitar enthusiast with basic instrument experience, I have tried to explore possibilities of composing small pieces of music.
Attached is a copy of small music that I composed a while ago. It layers two guitar tracks that I recorded myself, with a few effects added in Cubase, a digital audio workstation.

title: Anirban Chakraborty
text:
I am a postdoctoral scholar in the Department of Public Health Sciences at the Medical University of South Carolina, working with Dr. Souvik Seal. I develop statistical methods for single-cell and spatial omics, with a focus on biomarker discovery and replicate-aware multi-sample analysis, building on a background in scalable Bayesian methods for spatial data.
I received my Ph.D. in Statistics from Texas A&M University (2024), advised by Dr. Matthias Katzfuss.

Research interests

Biomarker discovery in single-cell and spatial omics
Multi-sample spatial omics and spatially aware dimension reduction
Scalable Gaussian processes and Bayesian computation
